messages:
Sophie L: Heads up — ACME flagged a p99 spike (~1.3s) on /generate for the last 30m and intermittent 'OOM during token generation' errors. They attached trace id T-abc123 and a small log snippet: 
[2026-03-17T14:02:10Z] OOM: failed alloc 324MB (requested contig)

InfraBot: :rotating_light: Incident created INC-4801234567. Auto-collected GPU+kv stats and traces (see attached).

Ryan M: Any recent runtime/allocator changes deployed in the past 12h to hosted-tier3?

Priya K: Support pulled tenant logs. KV per-process growth: peaked ~1.4GB on several workers. Looks correlated with many long-lived chat sessions w/o pruning.

Sophie L: nvidia-smi shows GPU memory at ~92% on worker-7 and worker-9; also seeing a lot of reserved fragments. We did roll out the q4 quantization to hosted-tier3 ~6h ago.

Ryan M: Quick triage: ran `gpu_allocator_stat --slabs=summary` on host-7 — Freeable fragments ~620MB, largest contiguous free block ~18MB. That explains the tail latency + allocation failures for medium-sized buffers. KV page count also up (alloc churn).

Priya K: ACME wants an immediate workaround — they prefer routing or rollback if needed.

Ryan M: Short-term mitigation plan: 1) Route ACME traffic off the most-fragmented hosts to fresh processes (avoid forced OOMs). 2) Trigger aggressive KV eviction for sessions idle >5m. 3) Apply allocator tuning: `allocator.redispatch=2` and lower `kv.eviction_threshold` to 0.78 for the tenant. 4) If symptoms persist, rollback the q4 rollout for ACME's model to last-good.

Sophie L: Can you paste the exact commands for redispatch / kv eviction so support can perform with minimal changes?

Ryan M: Commands:
`rctl set runtime.redispatch=2 --service=hosted-tier3`
`rctl set kv.eviction_threshold=0.78 --tenant=acme`
`kvctl evict --tenant acme --older-than 300s`
and to reclaim fragmentation on a host: `systemctl restart redwood-worker@host-7` (drain first, graceful).

InfraBot: Change request queued CHG-4801234580. Expected apply in ~10m once approvals pass.

Priya K: I ran `kvctl evict --tenant acme --older-than 300s` on the affected shard and it freed ~1.1GB of KV memory. Observability updates: p95 dropped from ~540ms -> ~220ms, p99 from ~1.3s -> ~410ms within ~6 minutes after eviction + routing.

Sophie L: :tada: ACME confirms latency back to baseline and no new OOMs for 20m. They asked for a durable fix and notes they see many long sessions from a batch import job.

Ryan M: Next steps: open a runtime PR to 1) add automatic KV pruning for sessions idle >X, 2) make `allocator.redispatch` toggle during high-frag signals (default bump 1->2), and 3) add a scheduled nightly rolling restart option for hot hosts to mitigate long-term fragmentation. I'll draft the RFC.

Priya K: I'll follow up with ACME about dedicated capacity options and the proposed tenant-side session retention settings.

Sophie L: Owners: Ryan = runtime fixes + RFC, Priya = customer comms. Marking this thread resolved for now; will monitor metrics for 2h and reopen if we see reoccurrence. Thanks all.
